title: More than water: How PepsiCo is helping communities build long-term resilience
summary: Through local programs, PepsiCo is aiming to expand access to safe water in communities where time, reliability, resilience and opportunity are deeply connected.
body_markdown:
## More than water: Reliable water can unlock education and opportunity


Water access can also shape opportunity. When communities have the tools and knowledge to manage water more reliably, the benefits can extend from household routines to education, livelihoods and local leadership.


At Ojodu Junior High School in Lagos State, Nigeria, access to water is closely tied to the basics of learning. Without reliable water, handwashing is harder, sanitation facilities are less safe, and students can lose time and confidence in the classroom environment. A solar-powered system developed with WaterAid and support from the PepsiCo Foundation has helped bring cleaner water and improved sanitation to the school, making the school day more predictable for students and staff.


Since 2022, the PepsiCo Foundation's partnership with WaterAid Nigeria has moved far beyond a single school project to reshape how an entire community accesses water. Across Lagos State, the partnership has built water facilities, sanitation facilities, drinking water stations and handwashing facilities, delivering direct access to clean water and sanitation for schools, communities and a primary health center. The change goes deeper than infrastructure: women trained as area mechanics now operate and maintain these systems as a source of livelihood, while the partnership helped Ikorodu North Local Council Development Authority build Lagos' first WASH Investment Plan, a long-term budgeting and asset-management tool now anchoring government advocacy for sustained water and sanitation funding. Together, these efforts show a program that has grown from isolated fixes into a lasting, locally owned system for water security in Lagos.
